A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–J are readable and matchable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and MNIST experiments, including early-termination comparisons and termination-threshold/load-balancing analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds original CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny ImageNet results, including accuracy comparisons.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same routing rule, expert updates, locality and auxiliary losses, and early-termination mechanism. ResNet-18 is introduced as a backbone for added experiments, without changing the proposed MoE procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from synthetic regression and MNIST to selected natural-image classes: four CIFAR-10 classes, six CIFAR-100 classes, and six Tiny ImageNet classes. MNIST remains in Appendix A.4 rather than being removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons remain single-expert learning and MoE configurations with and without early termination. Existing experiments retain their comparator membership; the added benchmarks introduce no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Added image experiments introduce ResNet-18, Adam, five epochs per round, new sample budgets, 300–350 rounds, and accuracy metrics. Retained MNIST is redescribed as N=60 tasks in K=3 clusters instead of N=3, without establishing a rerun; synthetic N=7 is corrected to 6. Some new settings remain ambiguous: Appendix A.5 states N=350, whereas Figure 6 states N=6.

E4.justification: V3 substantially extends tests of early termination and expert count to natural-image tasks, using paired termination/no-termination curves and accuracy comparisons in Figures 3–4 and 6–7 and Tables 1–2. The existing synthetic threshold and load-balancing analyses are retained as Figures 8–9.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 repetitions for the synthetic threshold experiment, shown in v2 Figure 5 and v3 Figure 9. V3 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for the added experiments.

E6.justification: V3 adds natural-image learning curves and average incremental accuracy results. Table 1 reports CIFAR-100 accuracy of 32.9% for M=10 versus 9.1% without early termination; Table 2 reports Tiny ImageNet accuracy of 37.6% for M=8 versus 10.5% without termination. These are new benchmark results; the retained synthetic and MNIST curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 restricts σ₀ from σ₀>0 to 0<σ₀<1. Appendix E.7 also changes the Lemma 13 proof bound from the norm of θ(T2)−θ(T1+1) to the norm of θ(T2). The principal theorem statements and remaining derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The central claims remain expert specialization, balanced routing, necessary gate-update termination, and forgetting/generalization benefits. The conclusion's added statement that more experts need not improve performance already appeared in v2's abstract and introduction.

C2.justification: The explicit restriction 0<σ₀<1 narrows the stated applicability of the analysis. Otherwise, interpretations of specialization, gate collapse, load balancing, expert count, and the top-k routing tradeoff remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds substantial reproducibility information for the new experiments, including class subsets, sample counts, ResNet-18 initialization, Adam settings, batch size, weight decay, and learning-rate scheduling. Hardware reporting changes from macOS/Intel graphics to Red Hat Linux/Xeon/V100; the earlier execution-time estimates are removed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds discussion of statistical MoE theory and Bayesian task-free continual learning, including Nguyen and Chamroukhi and Lee et al. Additional references support linear-model generalization and sparse routing. These are limited expansions within the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact, with localized rewriting and corrections. Appendix A gains dataset-specific subsections, MNIST moves there, and v3 adds acknowledgments and updates author affiliations and conference text.

P2.justification: V3 adds natural-image error, forgetting, and accuracy plots plus two accuracy tables, substantially expanding the empirical presentation. V2 Figure 3 moves to v3 Figure 5, and Figures 4–5 become Figures 8–9. The ICLR template also changes headers, author layout, typography, and algorithm placement.

improvement.justification: The added ResNet-18 experiments on selected natural-image classes strengthen support for extending the linear-model insights beyond MNIST, while accuracy tables make early-termination comparisons clearer. The overall gain is limited by conflicting task counts in appendix text and captions, absent uncertainty estimates for the new results, and removal of runtime information; the central theoretical contribution remains largely unchanged.
